items.title: FPL GW7 Transfer Tips! | Buy, Sell, Keep, Avoid #fpl
items.headline: Buy Bryan Mbeumo for the attacking upside, but hold Bukayo Saka through Gameweek 7
items.summary:
Bryan Mbeumo is the recommended Gameweek 7 buy, with the case centred on exploiting a favourable upcoming run that begins against Ipswich and continues with Aston Villa and Brighton. The latter two sides are allowing plenty of chances, while Manchester City’s strong projected goal numbers make an additional City attacker appealing alongside the widely owned Erling Haaland. Ipswich is viewed as the ideal entry point, although any City option carries a degree of rotation risk.

Yoane Wissa is the suggested sale. He is playing far deeper than an FPL forward should, is contributing little in advanced areas and is also being substituted early, raising concerns over both his role and minutes. With the Coventry fixture now gone, moving his place to another attacking option is advised; Callum Wilson is a leading replacement target for managers who do not already own João Pedro.

Bukayo Saka remains a firm hold despite frustration in Gameweek 6. He follows that blank with a goal and assist in the Champions League, and his underlying numbers and positions continue to look excellent. Saka is getting into dangerous areas consistently, passes the eye test and appears likely to convert his chance volume into attacking returns soon.

Nicolas Jackson is the forward to avoid despite scoring twice in two matches. His price is considered too high relative to other attractive striker options, while difficult fixtures against Newcastle away and Manchester City reduce the immediate appeal. Aston Villa’s attack is only beginning to click, so there is no need to rush into their assets either. James Tarkowski and Matheus Cunha are additional players to avoid.
key_points: Buy Bryan Mbeumo for Gameweek 7, targeting the Ipswich, Aston Villa and Brighton fixtures.
Consider a second Manchester City attacker alongside Erling Haaland, but account for occasional rotation.
Sell Yoane Wissa because his deeper role, limited attacking involvement and early substitutions weaken his FPL appeal.
Callum Wilson is a preferred Wissa replacement for managers without João Pedro.
Keep Bukayo Saka: his underlying numbers, advanced positions and recent Champions League return point to future FPL returns.
Avoid Nicolas Jackson despite two goals in two matches, with Newcastle away and Manchester City next.
James Tarkowski and Matheus Cunha are also flagged as avoid options.

items.title: FPL WATCHLIST GW7 WITH FPL HARRY 🔎 | BARRY, DE CUYPER & SAKA | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Bukayo Saka’s elite underlying numbers keep him ahead of Cole Palmer for Gameweek 7
items.summary:
Bukayo Saka remains the preferred premium midfielder over Cole Palmer despite Palmer returning eight points in Chelsea’s 5-1 win. Saka leads midfielders for expected goal involvement, big chances and shots on target, while his role has become notably more central and goal-focused. Mikel Arteta’s stated desire for Saka to target one or two goals every match supports the underlying data, and Saka’s apparent rest from Champions League starts protects his Premier League minutes. Palmer has the upside of a Chelsea side capable of scoring heavily, especially in marquee home matches, but his league data is unusually weak and Joao Pedro is viewed as Chelsea’s standout FPL asset.

Defence is the key transfer area ahead of Gameweek 7. Dipper remains a high-upside buy for Brighton’s home fixture against Crystal Palace, who have conceded the league’s highest xG, but his subsequent away games at Liverpool and Manchester City make him unsuitable for managers without bench cover. Brighton’s Dipper offers attacking potential from a left-wing role, although Mitoma and Minteh returning after the next international break could threaten his position. For a defender needed every week, Leeds’ Mormovic and Spurs’ Van Hecke are safer alternatives because of their reliable minutes, clean-sheet potential and favourable fixture runs.

Newcastle defenders are under major scrutiny after conceding four against Coventry. Lewis Hall still has attacking appeal, but poor defensive numbers and Newcastle’s performance make him a potential sale, with Vuskovic a viable replacement. Vuskovic is also a strong pick in his own right, combining clean-sheet, defensive-contribution and goal-threat routes, even if Dipper’s extraordinary short-term attacking role has made him the more explosive option. Manchester City defenders, including Gvardiol and O’Reilly, are harder to trust because rotation remains a concern despite Ipswich at home appearing attractive.

Among budget forwards, Dominic Calvert-Lewin is preferred to Barry and Yoane Wissa. Barry continues to receive an exceptional volume of big chances but misses too many of them, damaging both his reliability and bonus-point potential; he is worth holding for Chelsea if already owned, but not the priority purchase. Calvert-Lewin offers penalties, secure 90-minute starts, bonus potential and greater confidence in Leeds’ attack, making the ideal long-term third forward alongside Erling Haaland and Joao Pedro. Wissa is a more urgent sell after another limited-minute outing, poor data and the looming return of Osula. Joao Pedro is the priority upgrade for Gonzalo Garcia owners, while Kevin Schade’s shoulder injury, expected to keep him out until late November, creates a midfield transfer decision between short-term Newcastle coverage through Barnes and the longer-term Bournemouth appeal of Tavernier or Belumi.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 7, with Joao Pedro regarded as the best Chelsea attacker but not secure enough in minutes to rival Haaland for the armband.
Keep Bukayo Saka over Cole Palmer: Saka leads midfielders for xGI, big chances and shots on target, and is playing in more central scoring positions.
Buy Dipper for Crystal Palace at home only if a strong bench can cover Brighton’s following trips to Liverpool and Manchester City.
Prioritise Mormovic or Van Hecke over Dipper if the new defender must start in all of the next three gameweeks.
Newcastle’s defensive display against Coventry increases the case for selling Lewis Hall, with Vuskovic a strong replacement option.
Sell Yoane Wissa if possible, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin the preferred budget-forward replacement because of penalties, minutes and bonus potential.
Hold Barry if already owned for Chelsea, but avoid buying him over Calvert-Lewin because his wasteful finishing limits his FPL ceiling.
Kevin Schade’s shoulder injury is expected to rule him out until late November; Barnes, Tavernier and Belumi are the main midfield replacements under consideration.

items.title: FPL GW7 EXPERT Transfer Trends & Best Captain! 🧠 100 Experts Reveal Gameweek 7 Team Plans
items.headline: Haaland is the overwhelming Gameweek 7 captain as experts target Diper and Chery
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the clear Gameweek 7 captaincy call, with 97% of the surveyed experts backing him at home to Ipswich. That level of agreement is exceptionally rare, and the recommendation is not to overthink the armband: managers without Haaland face a strong case to buy him simply to access the captaincy. The tiny minority going elsewhere turn to Chery, Diper or Pascal Gross, but there is no meaningful alternative captain trend.

Almost half of experts roll a transfer, although 34% make one move and 14% make two. Many managers have accumulated three to five free transfers, so transfer activity is expected to increase over the coming weeks. The biggest buying trends are Diper, whose appeal is Crystal Palace at home, and Chery, who offers a more differential route into a favourable run that includes Ipswich at home. Calvert-Lewin is also strongly backed despite less interest from the wider game, while Gross, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers are increasingly treated as near-essential picks.

The main sales are Solay and Wissa. Solay’s expert ownership is projected to fall from 33% to 18%, while more than half of Wissa’s owners are set to sell, making moves such as Solay to Gross or Rogers and Wissa to Joao Pedro straightforward upgrades. Lewis Hall, Martin Odegaard, Sangare and Barry also attract some sales. Morgan Gibbs-White is a more cautious sell: only 5% of his expert owners move him on, with his upcoming fixtures making him a reasonable hold or bench option rather than an urgent exit.

The emerging expert template contains Kinsky and Vogen in goal; Calafiori, Konsa, Diper, Hall and Mahravic at the back; Gross, Rogers, Palmer, Saka and Gibbs-White in midfield; and Haaland, Joao Pedro and Calvert-Lewin up front. Cheap enablers including Barry, King, Thomas, Egan, Drava and Slater help finance the premium-heavy squad. Chip use is limited outside bench boost, which is used by 7% of experts; that suggests Gameweek 7 is viable for managers already set up with a strong playing bench. Only 4% use triple captain, with many holding it for a later Haaland opportunity, while free hit and wildcard usage is negligible.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Ipswich at home; 97% of experts give him the armband in Gameweek 7.
Diper is the leading transfer target, with Crystal Palace at home driving the move.
Chery is the main expert differential, offering a way to gain from the favourable fixture run beyond simply owning Haaland.
Sell candidates are Solay and Wissa, with Gross, Rogers and Joao Pedro the most logical replacement targets.
Keep or bench Morgan Gibbs-White rather than selling hastily, as 95% of his expert owners retain him.
Calvert-Lewin, Gross, Joao Pedro and Rogers continue to gain expert ownership and are approaching template status.
Bench boost is used by 7% of experts, but triple captain, wildcard and free hit are largely being saved.

items.title: My transfer tips ahead of Gameweek 7 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Move on Florian Wirtz and target Dominic Calvert-Lewin for the Gameweek 7 reset
items.summary:
Florian Wirtz looks like a sensible sell ahead of Gameweek 7, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the preferred long-term forward replacement. Wissa is another player worth moving on after looking poor, operating away from the No. 9 role and being substituted early in Gameweek 6. Gonzalo García is the attractive short-term alternative for the next two fixtures, but Calvert-Lewin offers the stronger longer-term case.

Bournemouth injury news needs monitoring before committing to their assets. Iraola expects players including Isak and Gakpo to be back soon, potentially not in time for Gameweek 7 but more likely for Gameweek 8. For a Manchester City attacker beyond Erling Haaland, Turkey is preferred, although Semenyo appears to offer the safer minutes. There is no need to fear stacking attacking players from one side: Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Morgan Rogers are all strong selections individually, so they remain viable together.

Alfury remains a strong pick despite another Champions League rest, as that rotation increasingly looks like a pattern that protects him for league minutes. Morgan Gibbs-White is a clear hold, with Ipswich away in Gameweek 8 a favourable fixture. Pascal Groß is still a viable buy even with Liverpool and Manchester City in Gameweeks 8 and 9, while Savio is an appealing differential punt for Coventry at home this week.

In defence, Lewis Hall should not be sold in panic because his attacking upside makes him playable in better fixtures and benchable in difficult ones. Chia is more expendable, with Jan Paul van Hecke the leading defensive target for Gameweek 7. Silva at Bournemouth is another option, particularly for defensive-contribution potential. Budget midfielders include Balumi at £5.2m, who should continue to start, and Rodoni at Coventry for £4.9m, with possible penalty duties; Yan Out is also useful but sits one yellow card from a suspension.
key_points: Florian Wirtz is a sell candidate ahead of Gameweek 7, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin the preferred long-term replacement.
Sell Wissa if a transfer is available after his poor form, reduced central role and early Gameweek 6 substitution.
Gonzalo García is a strong two-week forward punt, while Calvert-Lewin is the better durable transfer.
Hold Morgan Gibbs-White for Ipswich away in Gameweek 8.
Do not rush to sell Lewis Hall; his attacking threat justifies keeping him as a rotating defender.
Jan Paul van Hecke is the preferred defender to buy this week, with Bournemouth's Silva also a useful defensive-contributions option.
Savio is a differential midfield punt for Coventry at home, while Pascal Groß remains buyable despite Liverpool and Manchester City in Gameweeks 8 and 9.
Monitor Bournemouth team news: Iraola expects Isak and Gakpo back by Gameweek 8 if they do not return for Gameweek 7.

items.title: MY FPL GW7 TRANSFER TARGETS! ♻️  Szoboszlai + Wissa Replacements | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Morgan Rogers tops Gameweek 7 transfer list as Haaland and João Pedro remain essential
items.summary:
Morgan Rogers is the standout Gameweek 7 midfield buy, combining stronger underlying numbers than Cole Palmer with a lower price than both Palmer and Bukayo Saka. He is viewed as a long-term hold rather than a short-term fixture punt, with the recommendation to buy despite recent price rises. Palmer is narrowly preferred to Saka for the immediate period because Chelsea have kinder fixtures and no European football, while Arsenal’s Champions League schedule raises the prospect of heavier minutes and rotation for Saka. Pascal Groß also remains part of a strong, increasingly template midfield core alongside Rogers and either Palmer or Saka.

At the back, Riccardo Calafiori is the leading target. Arsenal’s defensive outlook remains strong, his attacking threat justifies a £5.9m price, and a possible injury to Hincapié strengthens his appeal. David Raya remains a solid alternative route into Arsenal’s defence, while Cristhian Mosquera is only a short-term option because William Saliba is expected back around Gameweek 11. Brighton defenders are attractive longer term despite difficult trips to Liverpool and Manchester City in two of the next three: Lewis Dunk offers the greater attacking upside, while Vuskovic is the steadier choice. Leeds’ Mephamovic is the preferred budget defender because of strong defensive-contribution data, favourable fixtures and no European rotation risk, with James Justin a cheaper but slightly less secure route in.

Bournemouth, Manchester City and Leeds have the most appealing fixture runs over the next six weeks. Bournemouth attackers such as Marcus Tavernier, Silva and Evanilson become viable, although European commitments and Alex Scott’s absence weaken confidence in their defence after conceding five against Chelsea. Tavernier is especially appealing while Kluivert is injured because he has penalties, though Krepin Diatta’s expected return could affect that. Manchester City assets beyond Erling Haaland, including Rayan Cherki, Semenyo and O’Riley, carry significant minutes uncertainty. Leeds are backed as a strong side with good rotation-friendly fixtures, making Calvert-Lewin a particularly attractive £6m forward ahead of Manchester United at home.

Haaland and João Pedro are considered near-essential forwards: Haaland remains too reliable to sell for premium midfield investment, while João Pedro has strong data, form and secure minutes without European football. Calvert-Lewin is the best third-forward purchase, with Manchester United, Sunderland, Bournemouth and Spurs next and no midweek schedule. Everton’s Doucouré is a secondary option from Gameweek 9, but his missed big chances and weak bonus potential make Calvert-Lewin preferable. Managers unconvinced by the forward pool should instead buy a £4.5m bench forward and play 3-5-2 or 4-4-2, rather than chase inconsistent options such as Evan Ferguson, Yoane Wissa or Dominic Solanke.
key_points: Buy Morgan Rogers as the priority Gameweek 7 midfielder; his price, data and long-term prospects put him ahead of Cole Palmer and Bukayo Saka.
Captaincy and premium structure should continue to centre on Erling Haaland, who is not considered a worthwhile sell for inconsistent premium midfielders.
João Pedro is treated as essential because of his performances, underlying numbers and lack of European rotation risk.
Riccardo Calafiori is the top defensive transfer, with Arsenal’s fixtures and his attacking threat offsetting his £5.9m cost.
Lewis Dunk is the high-upside Brighton defender, while Vuskovic offers a safer long-term alternative despite Brighton’s difficult short-term fixtures.
Leeds’ Mephamovic and forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin benefit from favourable fixtures and no European football; Calvert-Lewin faces Manchester United, Sunderland, Bournemouth and Spurs next.
Marcus Tavernier is a Bournemouth differential with penalties while Kluivert is injured, but Europe and Krepin Diatta’s possible return are risks.
Avoid forcing a third premium forward: a £4.5m striker and a 3-5-2 or 4-4-2 shape is preferred over unreliable options such as Wissa, Solanke and Evan Ferguson.

items.title: FPL Gameweek 7 Preview 🔥 Time for Wissa to go? ✅
items.headline: Calvert-Lewin edges Wissa as the cheap-forward move for Gameweek 7
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the clear captain for Manchester City’s home meeting with Ipswich in Gameweek 7, despite a demanding Liverpool-PSG-Ipswich sequence and the possibility of an early substitution. City have easier upcoming opportunities to rest him, while Arsenal’s Bukayo Saka is the preferred alternative over Cole Palmer and Bruno Fernandes if Haaland is unavailable. Saka, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Riccardo Calafiori are rested in Europe, strengthening their Premier League minutes outlook; Saka also returns from the bench with a goal and assist and is expected to retain penalties while Havertz is fit.

A Gameweek 7 Free Hit is not especially compelling because many managers already own Arsenal, Chelsea and Brighton assets with acceptable fixtures. A fixtures-led draft leans heavily on Manchester City, Brighton, Spurs and Fulham, but it carries major differential risk through players such as Savio, Mohammed Kudus and Brighton defenders. The stronger long-term Wildcard structure is built around Chelsea’s Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro; Arsenal’s David Raya, Calafiori and Saka; Brighton’s Bart Verbruggen and Pascal Gross; plus Haaland and Dominic Calvert-Lewin. Chelsea’s run through Gameweek 13 is strong and their lack of European football supports the security of their core players, while Calafiori offers better value than Gabriel given his price and improving minutes.

Newcastle assets are increasingly difficult to trust after another 4-1 defeat, this time against Coventry. Yoane Wissa plays as a No. 10 rather than a central striker, is substituted on 77 minutes and now carries more concern over role and minutes, although he remains a reasonable short-term hold for Aston Villa at home if managers have only one free transfer. Harvey Barnes is safer to hold because his minutes remain stronger, but is not a buy; Fabian Schar is a sell when convenient, while Lewis Hall can be benched or retained because his attacking upside gives him a route to returns even without clean sheets.

Calvert-Lewin is the leading Wissa replacement ahead of Gonzalo Garcia and Barry. Garcia is the better short-term punt for Hull and Coventry, but Fulham’s form is unconvincing, whereas Calvert-Lewin offers reliable starts, penalties, no European rotation and a sustained run of playable Leeds fixtures. Barry is attractive at a lower price and has elite early xG numbers, but Chelsea and Arsenal in the next two Gameweeks make him harder to start. In midfield, Gross remains the best long-term budget option despite Liverpool and City in the next three, Savio is the preferred Spurs punt, and Tyler is appealing but carries European-rotation and early-substitution concerns. Morgan Gibbs-White should be held for Ipswich in Gameweek 8 and is a viable long-term £8m midfielder because he is nailed, on penalties, avoids Europe and offers bonus-point potential.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Ipswich in Gameweek 7; Saka is the best non-Haaland alternative, ahead of Palmer and Bruno Fernandes.
Saka, Odegaard, Havertz and Calafiori are rested in Arsenal’s midweek match, improving their Gameweek 7 minutes prospects.
Avoid buying Ben White or Jurrien Timber, while Calafiori is the preferred Arsenal defender over Gabriel on value and expected minutes.
A Gameweek 7 Free Hit is difficult to justify if managers already own Arsenal, Chelsea and Brighton players with good fixtures.
Sell Wissa when transfers allow, but with only one free transfer he can be held for Aston Villa at home rather than forcing a move.
Calvert-Lewin is the preferred cheap forward for security of starts, penalties and fixtures; Gonzalo Garcia is the shorter-term alternative and Barry suits tight budgets.
Pascal Gross remains the leading cheap midfield buy, Savio is the upside Spurs punt, and Tyler’s early substitutions and European schedule add risk.
Keep Gibbs-White through Ipswich in Gameweek 8; his penalties, durability, secure minutes and lack of European football make him a strong longer-term option.

items.title: FPL DEFCON DEEP DIVE WITH TOM HADLEY 📝 | GAMEWEEK 7 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Bobby Thomas and Moramovic lead the DefCon defender targets as Kyper ownership pressure grows
items.summary:
Bobby Thomas emerges as the standout budget defender after posting 20 defensive-contribution points in Coventry’s 4-1 win over Newcastle. The £4.0m centre-back is already a strong DefCon option, with three goal-line clearances in six gameweeks, regular shooting threat and a fixture run of Fulham, Sunderland, Everton and Crystal Palace after Tottenham. Coventry look more competitive than expected, particularly at home, so Thomas is recommended as both a cheap rotation defender and a Wildcard pick rather than simply a bench filler.

Moramovic is the preferred higher-priced defensive signing for managers needing a player they can start most weeks. Leeds remain defensively organised, he offers set-piece and attacking threat, and he still returns two points against Arsenal despite conceding twice and receiving a booking. His upcoming matches against Manchester United, Sunderland, Bournemouth and Tottenham are playable, with only Chelsea away looking like a likely benching fixture. Silva remains a viable alternative for Bournemouth, but their defensive display against Chelsea creates more concern; doubling up with Tavernier also weakens the case for managers who already own the midfielder.

Other DefCon names to monitor include Everton’s James Tarkowski and Jarrad Branthwaite, Spurs’ Van Hecke, Nottingham Forest’s Murillo and Bournemouth’s Hill. Murillo is the leading regular DefCon scorer across the first six gameweeks and has even become the first defender to reach the threshold against Crystal Palace. Fixtures matter heavily: centre-backs facing Manchester United, Leeds, Brentford and Everton have produced particularly strong DefCon hit rates, making Liverpool defenders against Brentford and Chelsea defenders against Everton potential short-term plays, although Chelsea’s long run of concessions remains a major clean-sheet risk.

In midfield, the most reliable cheap defensive-contribution options remain Manchester United’s Kobbie Mainoo and Brentford’s Janelt, while Everton’s James Garner offers a more expensive but steady route to points. Brighton’s Carlos Baleba is worth watching if his starts become secure after reaching 12 DefCon points in limited minutes. These players are especially useful for Bench Boosts, where their defensive floor can make a four-point return realistic even without attacking output.

Bonus data reinforces the appeal of several attacking players. Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer combine returns with strong baseline bonus potential, while João Pedro remains an excellent asset but relies more heavily on goals and assists. Manchester City’s Rayan Cherki and Jérémy Doku benefit from the revised dribble scoring in the bonus system, as unsuccessful take-ons no longer cancel successful ones; both can accumulate baseline points quickly if they start. The major ownership concern is Kyper, whose left-wing role, early substitutions and explosive output make him difficult to oppose, even though Vuskovic remains viewed as a strong longer-term defender in his own right.
key_points: Bobby Thomas is the leading £4.0m defender target after 20 DefCon points, a goal-line clearance habit and a favourable Coventry fixture run.
Moramovic is the preferred transfer-in for managers wanting a DefCon defender they can start through Leeds’ matches with Manchester United, Sunderland, Bournemouth and Tottenham.
Murillo leads the regular DefCon standings and is the only defender so far to hit the threshold against Crystal Palace.
Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Van Hecke and Hill remain viable defensive options, but Chelsea defenders carry clean-sheet risk despite a favourable Everton fixture.
Mainoo and Janelt provide cheap midfield DefCon cover, while James Garner offers a steadier but pricier Everton option.
Rogers and Palmer have strong baseline bonus profiles; João Pedro’s bonus appeal depends more on attacking returns.
Cherki and Doku gain from bonus-system treatment of successful dribbles, but Pep Guardiola’s rotation makes their minutes uncertain.
Kyper is a major effective-ownership threat because of his advanced role and frequent early substitutions, making non-owners nervous despite Vuskovic’s long-term appeal.

items.title: THE FPL SCOUTCAST GAMEWEEK 7 🚨| GW7 TEAM REVEALS | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Erling Haaland is the standout Triple Captain call for Manchester City’s Ipswich fixture
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the overwhelming captaincy favourite for Gameweek 7 as Manchester City host Ipswich, with the fixture also presenting a strong Triple Captain opportunity for managers still holding the chip. City lead the attacking projections over the next six gameweeks, while Ipswich rank among the weakest defences. The caveat is City’s Champions League tie with PSG: Haaland’s fitness and minutes there need monitoring, but if he comes through unscathed, the immediate certainty of his role makes Ipswich preferable to waiting for a later fixture such as Hull at home in Gameweek 16.

The recommended squad core remains double Arsenal defence, Haaland and Joao Pedro, with Riccardo Calafiori close to essential given his clean-sheet potential and attacking threat. Arsenal’s Gameweek 7 trip to Nottingham Forest is appealing, especially as Forest have failed to score in their last three home matches. Spurs also have favourable defensive projections, notably Coventry at home in Gameweek 7, Crystal Palace in Gameweek 9 and Ipswich in Gameweek 11, but their inconsistency makes Micky van de Ven or Guglielmo Vicario-style investment a risk rather than a certainty.

In defence, Maxime Esteve? No: Bournemouth’s Antonio Silva and Brighton’s Jan Paul van Hecke are the more interesting medium-term picks because they combine defensive-contribution potential with good fixture runs. Silva offers a route into Bournemouth’s Sunderland, Leeds, Ipswich, Forest, Fulham and Hull sequence, but European commitments, injuries to key teammates and Bournemouth’s 5-1 defeat to Chelsea reduce confidence. Van Hecke, now below £5.0m, has a long run of usable fixtures and can be rotated in tougher away games. Crystal Palace’s Maxence Lacroix also posts strong attacking and defensive-contribution numbers, but Palace’s European schedule and a £5.0m price make him a wait-and-see option.

Up front, Thierno Barry’s underlying numbers remain excellent: he ranks third for expected goal involvement over the last six gameweeks and generates a huge volume of chances. However, his finishing is unreliable and Everton’s fixture run worsens, so he is easier to own as a benchable £5.7m forward than as a weekly starter. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the preferred replacement in the £6.0m bracket, with penalties, secure minutes and Leeds fixtures that improve sharply after Manchester United in Gameweek 7. Fulham’s Gonzalo Garcia is useful for the immediate Hull and Coventry games but looks like a short-term transfer; Nicolas Jackson is an interesting Aston Villa punt but costs too much for a third forward.

Managers with a free transfer are generally encouraged to avoid unnecessary reshaping. A move from Harry Maguire or Kristoffer Ajer to Manchester City’s Daouda? No: to City defender Doku? The clearest defensive upgrade discussed is Maguire to Manchester City’s Decoiper, whose out-of-position role looks secure and whose attacking returns justify playing him against Palace. In midfield, Rayan Cherki is the high-upside City option for the next run, though his minutes are less secure than Morgan Rogers’. If Liverpool’s Dominik Szoboszlai remains absent, a switch to Rogers is the safer long-term move; cheaper City midfielders Nico O’Reilly? No: Anderson or Enzo Fernandez offer steady minutes, with Anderson preferred for defensive contributions and set-piece involvement.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Ipswich in Gameweek 7, and consider using Triple Captain if he emerges fit from Manchester City’s PSG match.
Calvert-Lewin is the preferred £6.0m forward over Barry, Garcia and Solanke because he has penalties, reliable minutes and Leeds’ improving fixture run.
Barry remains a viable cheap forward because of elite chance volume, but his poor finishing and Everton’s tougher fixtures make him a rotation option.
Keep Calafiori and Arsenal defensive coverage for Nottingham Forest away, with Forest scoreless in their last three home matches.
Van Hecke is a strong sub-£5.0m defensive target due to Brighton’s fixture run, while Antonio Silva carries more European-rotation and team-stability risk.
Cherki is the high-ceiling second Manchester City attacker, but Morgan Rogers is the safer minutes pick if Szoboszlai needs replacing.
Spurs defenders have strong projected clean-sheet fixtures, but their volatile performances make double Spurs defence a high-risk play.
Monitor Joao Pedro, Cherki and Haaland through midweek European matches before making early transfers.

items.title: MY FPL GW7 FIRST TRANSFER PLANS! 📝 Gibbs-White vs Hall 🤔 #fpl #premierleague
items.headline: Haaland captained as post-Wildcard squad banks a Gameweek 7 transfer
items.summary:
The Gameweek 7 plan is to stick with a 4-3-3 after deploying the Wildcard last week and to avoid an unnecessary early transfer. The squad carries five strong defenders, four of whom have favourable fixtures, so Maxim De Cuyper, Riccardo Calafiori, Lewis Hall and Jan Paul van Hecke start. De Cuyper comes in after a 15-point haul, while Van Hecke is preferred for his attacking potential and defensive-contribution appeal despite Tottenham’s encouraging defensive start to the season.

Morgan Gibbs-White is first substitute rather than starting at home to Arsenal. Arsenal remain the league’s standout defence, and Nottingham Forest have not looked convincing enough to justify benching one of the selected attackers or defenders. Gibbs-White has had opportunities, but the lack of finishing around him limits confidence in his immediate upside. The £4.5m midfielder Slater stays on the bench, while Mahmovic, at home to Manchester United, offers emergency cover if required.

Rolling the free transfer is the priority in the week immediately after the Wildcard. A move only becomes necessary if multiple injuries force the issue, as the existing XI is considered strong enough to play. Keeping the transfer creates flexibility for the following gameweek rather than chasing a marginal one-week gain.

Erling Haaland is the captain at home to Fulham, with João Pedro handed the vice-captaincy after his strong form at Everton. Bukayo Saka remains in the squad for now, although a future switch to Cole Palmer is under consideration. That move is not rushed in Gameweek 7 because it cannot be funded as a straightforward one-for-one transfer and the spare transfer is more valuable than forcing the change.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland at home to Fulham, with João Pedro as vice-captain.
Start De Cuyper, Calafiori, Lewis Hall and Van Hecke in a 4-3-3 after the Wildcard.
Bench Morgan Gibbs-White against Arsenal, with Slater also among the substitutes.
Van Hecke starts because his attacking threat and defensive-contribution potential outweigh concerns over Tottenham’s defensive form.
Roll the Gameweek 7 free transfer unless injuries create a genuine need to act.
Keep Saka for now; a move to Cole Palmer is a future possibility but requires additional funds or transfers.

items.title: FPL GAMEWEEK 7 PREVIEW! 🔮 SELLING NEWCASTLE? BUYING MAN CITY? ♻️ | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Haaland is the standout Triple Captain call for Ipswich visit in Gameweek 7
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the leading captaincy option for Gameweek 7 as Manchester City host Ipswich. City have scored three against Liverpool and look increasingly fluent in attack, while Ipswich have conceded plenty of chances despite their numbers being distorted by Manchester United posting almost 5.0 xG against them earlier in the season. The Triple Captain chip is viable on Haaland, with later home fixtures against Fulham in Gameweek 11 and Hull in Gameweek 16 alternatives, but Christmas rotation risk makes this immediate opportunity especially appealing.

Newcastle’s 4-1 defeat at Coventry is alarming, particularly given poor underlying numbers: they rank 16th for xG and 18th for expected goals conceded despite a favourable opening run. However, Aston Villa, Crystal Palace, Everton and Fulham follow, and Lewis Hall and Malik Chow still offer DefCon and attacking value. Managers with only one or two free transfers are advised to hold Newcastle assets for Aston Villa at home, while those with three or four transfers can reasonably move early. Yoane Wissa is also worth retaining because the main cheap forward replacements, Barry and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, have less appealing immediate fixtures.

Brighton players remain buyable even after their price rises. Diper and Pascal Gross face Crystal Palace at home before Liverpool and Manchester City away, but Brighton’s schedule turns highly favourable from Gameweek 10 through to around Gameweek 20. Gross is viewed as the safer long-term pick and can be started even in the difficult away fixtures. Diper has greater minutes risk once Ma and Mitoma return around Gameweek 11, although his current form could still earn him a lasting role. Vuskovic is a viable alternative for managers unwilling to chase Diper.

Bukayo Saka is preferred to Cole Palmer for now. Palmer returns eight points despite recording no shots, 0.0 xG and only 0.07 expected assists in Gameweek 6, whereas Arsenal are deliberately pushing Saka into more central and penalty-box positions. Saka’s shots and touches in the box are up, and Mikel Arteta wants him to become a more consistent goalscorer. Joao Pedro is considered Chelsea’s best captaincy asset, while Haaland remains the best overall captain. Manchester City attackers such as Cherki and Semenyo are attractive short-term punts for Ipswich but carry major rotation risk, with Doku fit again, Foden returning from suspension and several players competing for three spots.

A Free Hit can aggressively target City’s home fixture, using Haaland alongside Cherki and Semenyo if their Champions League minutes permit, plus Brighton, Spurs and Arsenal defensive coverage. A wildcard should not force differentials simply because the template is strong: build around Raya, Arsenal defensive cover, Gross, Saka, Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro, Calvert-Lewin and Haaland, retain squad depth and bank transfers for when the template changes.
key_points: Triple Captain Haaland is a strong Gameweek 7 play against Ipswich at the Etihad, ahead of potentially more rotation-prone later opportunities.
Hold Lewis Hall, Malik Chow and Wissa for Newcastle’s home match against Aston Villa unless you have several free transfers and a clear upgrade.
Newcastle’s underlying data is concerning, ranking 16th for xG and 18th for xG conceded, so another poor display against Aston Villa should trigger sales.
Pascal Gross remains a strong Brighton buy despite Liverpool and Manchester City away after Crystal Palace, with an excellent fixture run beginning in Gameweek 10.
Diper is still worth considering but faces increased minutes risk when Ma and Mitoma return around Gameweek 11; Vuskovic is an alternative.
Keep Saka over Palmer: Saka’s central positioning and improved box involvement are more encouraging than Palmer’s low underlying output in Gameweek 6.
Cherki and Semenyo can be short-term City punts against Ipswich, but Doku, Foden and other attackers make their starts difficult to predict.
Calvert-Lewin and Barry are the preferred cheap forward targets outside Haaland and Joao Pedro, with Calvert-Lewin favoured on immediate fixtures.

items.headline: Tavernier minutes cloud Bournemouth midfield transfer plans
items.summary:
Marcus Tavernier’s reduced minutes are viewed as a product of several factors rather than a simple loss of favour. Bournemouth have European commitments approaching, recent results have been poor, and the Chelsea match is effectively finished as a contest. Injuries also leave the squad stretched, with Alex Scott, Tavernier and Justin Kluivert forming much of the side’s attacking core, increasing the concern if another key player is sidelined.

Tavernier remains an uncertain FPL pick because his minutes carry risk, but the alternatives are hardly convincing. Emiliano Buendía, priced at £5.9m, is considered, although an away trip to Newcastle is unattractive and his early substitution adds another minutes warning. Rayan is another possible replacement, but does not inspire much confidence.

A more differential route is also under consideration. Garner, at £6.0m, has Chelsea at home, though doubling up with Barry against that opponent is not especially appealing. Christian Nørgaard at £4.8m is a cheaper defensive-contribution option if he returns to the side, but that role is still unconfirmed. The transfer decision therefore hinges on whether Tavernier’s situation improves, with each replacement carrying either fixture, minutes or upside concerns.
key_points: Tavernier’s minutes are a concern, with Europe, poor form, game-state management and Bournemouth injuries all contributing factors.
Bournemouth’s attacking depth is vulnerable if Tavernier joins Alex Scott and Justin Kluivert on the injury list.
Buendía costs £5.9m but faces Newcastle away and has recently been substituted early.
Garner at £6.0m is a differential candidate for Chelsea at home, but a double-up with Barry is viewed cautiously.
Nørgaard, at £4.8m, is a potential defensive-contribution option only if he regains his place in the team.

items.title: FPL GW7 Transfer Tips 🔥 Best Man City Midfielders to BUY ✅
items.headline: Cherki offers Manchester City upside, but Calvert-Lewin remains the safer Gameweek 7 buy
items.summary:
Manchester City’s home meeting with Ipswich in Gameweek 7 makes their midfielders tempting, but none is entirely straightforward. Rayan Cherki is the standout for attacking output at £7.8m, with excellent underlying numbers, but Phil Foden’s return creates a real minutes risk and Cherki could regularly be withdrawn early. Semenyo is the safer route for starts after playing 90 minutes in every league match, though his 0.06 expected goals so far offers little goal threat for £8.3m. Doku is an appealing cheaper punt after impressing against Liverpool, but competition from Jérémy Doku’s fellow wide options, including Ndiaye, makes his minutes uncertain. Enzo Fernández and Elliot Anderson are regular starters but lack enough attacking or DefCon appeal to justify their prices.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a hold rather than a buy. Nottingham Forest face Arsenal in Gameweek 7 before Ipswich in Gameweek 8, and the ideal buying window was before the recent run of Coventry, Crystal Palace and Ipswich. Existing owners should usually keep him for the Ipswich fixture because he is nailed for 90 minutes, takes penalties and has strong creative and bonus-point potential. Non-owners can look elsewhere, especially with Forest’s fixtures worsening after Ipswich. The same logic applies to Fulham’s Gonzalo García and Josh King: owners should retain them through Hull at home and Coventry away, but new buyers have missed one of the three promoted-team fixtures and face some uncertainty over a possible managerial change.

Aston Villa midfielders are better assessed from Gameweek 9, when their schedule turns strongly in their favour. Manzambi is the most exciting option at £5.9m, with encouraging expected-goal and assist numbers and rising minutes, but Villa’s Champions League commitments could expose rotation or early substitutions. John McGinn is reliable for starts at £5.4m but offers less appeal than penalty-taking Enzo Le Fée, while Buendía’s recent early substitutions make him difficult to trust. Arsenal assets remain attractive: Riccardo Calafiori is a priority buy below £6m if there is a spare Arsenal slot, combining first-choice left-back status, clean-sheet potential and strong attacking numbers. Piero Hincapié’s injury further helps his case, although Champions League team news is worth monitoring. Martin Ødegaard remains a reasonable hold despite recent blanks, as his 0.34 expected goals and 0.27 expected assists per 90 suggest returns should follow, but he is not essential for managers who already own two Arsenal players.

For budget enablers, Hull’s Balumi is a credible £5.2m eighth-attacker after scoring three times in six gameweeks; his recent benching is attributed to tiredness and he is expected to return to the side. Brentford’s Yanel offers regular DefCon points but sits one booking from a suspension, making Balumi the more attacking alternative. Up front, Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the preferred low-cost transfer. He is nailed, on penalties and faces a workable six-match run, while Leeds’ lack of European football removes rotation concerns. His finishing remains unreliable, but his chance volume is strong. Evanilson is a high-upside differential with excellent fixtures but similarly wasteful finishing, while Gonzalo García is still the better hold for current owners than a fresh purchase.
key_points: Captaincy and transfer interest in Manchester City should favour Cherki for upside or Semenyo for minutes, but both carry clear trade-offs.
Do not buy Morgan Gibbs-White before Arsenal away in Gameweek 7; current owners should hold for Ipswich in Gameweek 8.
Keep Gonzalo García and Josh King through Fulham’s matches against Hull and Coventry, but avoid chasing them as new transfers after the Ipswich blank.
Wait until Gameweek 9 to target Aston Villa midfielders, when fixtures improve and European-rotation information is clearer.
Calafiori is a strong Arsenal buy under £6m, particularly with Hincapié injured, provided Champions League minutes do not become excessive.
Ødegaard is a hold at £6.8m because his underlying numbers remain strong, but Saka, Raya, Calafiori and short-term option Kiwior can rank ahead of him as Arsenal picks.
Balumi is a useful £5.2m budget midfielder for an eighth-attacker role; Yanel is dependable for DefCon but is one yellow card from suspension.
Calvert-Lewin is the leading cheap-forward buy for Gameweek 7 due to secure starts, penalties and decent fixtures, with Evanilson a riskier differential.

items.title: FPL GW7 TRANSFER TIPS! | Top Picks Tier List for Gameweek 7 - 2026/27! ⭐
items.headline: João Pedro and Calafiori lead Gameweek 7 buying plans as Haaland becomes a Triple Captain contender
items.summary:
João Pedro is the standout forward buy for Gameweek 7 at £7.8m, combining strong underlying numbers, clinical finishing and a favourable enough fixture run to make a case for near-essential status. Erling Haaland is also a priority addition for managers without him ahead of Ipswich at home, with Triple Captain a viable consideration if he comes through Manchester City’s Champions League match unscathed. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a strong longer-term option despite underwhelming returns: his three shots, 2.7 box shots and one big chance per game suggest goals should follow, while Leeds’ schedule improves markedly from Gameweek 10. Solanke is the more differential route, with penalties and appealing Spurs fixtures including Coventry, Chelsea and Crystal Palace.

Among current forward owners, Gonzalo, Calvert-Lewin and Thiago are holds because their chance volume and penalty duties support patience. Barry remains playable, including against Chelsea, after matching Haaland for shot volume and exceeding him for big chances, but poor finishing and bonus-point potential make him expendable rather than a buy. Wissa can be retained if already owned but is not worth buying at £6.3m because he plays too deeply, while injured forwards Alexander Isak, Igor Jesus and Brobbey should generally be sold to release funds and avoid uncertain absences.

Pascal Gross is the leading midfield buy at £6m. His penalty role, attacking involvement for Brighton and Crystal Palace fixture make him exceptional value, even if recent output exceeds the underlying data. Rogers is another premium-value midfielder with strong numbers and form, while Tavernier offers a longer-term Bournemouth route through penalties, set pieces and improving fixtures. Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard are holds rather than urgent purchases; Arsenal’s upcoming games against Forest, Everton and Hull offer upside, and Saka is an early captaincy candidate for Gameweek 10. Manchester City midfielders Cherki and Doku are attractive Ipswich punts only after Champions League minutes clarify their rotation risk.

At the back, Riccardo Calafiori is the premier target, with Arsenal clean-sheet potential, sustained attacking threat and a favourable Premier League role. Arsenal defensive cover remains a priority, with Gabriel a safe four-week hold and Konsa a cheaper short-term buy while his place lasts. Antonio Silva is the preferred medium-term differential: Bournemouth’s results have been poor but their defensive data is more respectable, while Silva combines set-piece goal threat with strong defensive-contribution potential ahead of Sunderland, Leeds and Ipswich. De Cuyper is an elite one-week Gameweek 7 option against Crystal Palace but carries major risks thereafter, with Liverpool and Manchester City next and Brighton winger returns potentially reducing his advanced role. Raya remains the best goalkeeper, while Petrovic is the recommended £4.5m long-term alternative; Pickford and Henderson are sell candidates due to difficult fixtures and weak team defences.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Ipswich in Gameweek 7, with Triple Captain in consideration if he avoids a damaging Champions League workload.
Buy João Pedro as the leading forward target; he offers strong underlying numbers, form and a manageable price at £7.8m.
Hold Saka for Arsenal’s improving run and consider him as a Gameweek 10 captaincy option.
Gross and Rogers are the preferred midfield additions, with Tavernier a longer-term differential on penalties and set pieces.
Buy Calafiori for Arsenal’s clean-sheet odds and attacking role, while Gabriel remains a safe hold and Konsa is a short-term budget option.
Antonio Silva is the preferred medium-to-long-term defensive differential because of set-piece threat, defensive contributions and Bournemouth’s fixture swing.
Treat De Cuyper as a Gameweek 7-only punt rather than a long-term transfer because Brighton face Liverpool and Manchester City next and his role may change.
Sell injured Isak, Igor Jesus and Brobbey; move on from Pedro Porro, Reece James and Tarkowski, while Pickford is expendable at £5.5m before Everton’s difficult run.

items.headline: Erling Haaland is the standout Triple Captain play for Gameweek 7
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the clear premium focus ahead of Gameweek 7, with Manchester City apparently unlikely to face any immediate disruption from their charges. If the Triple Captain chip is still available, this is rated an excellent week to use it on Haaland. Alternative chip opportunities include Hull at home in Gameweek 16, Bukayo Saka against Hull in Gameweek 10, or Bruno Fernandes against Coventry in Gameweek 14, but Haaland is the preferred immediate option.

Despite five blanks in six gameweeks, Bruno Fernandes remains a hold unless selling him directly funds a more important move. Morgan Rogers continues to offer reliable value after returning in five of the first six gameweeks, while João Pedro is fit again and is considered a strong forward option going forward. Savio also merits attention after playing 390 consecutive minutes; he impresses against Manchester United despite no attacking return. The goalkeeper referred to as Kyper has 53 points in six gameweeks and is still worth buying for managers with spare transfers.

There are several fitness and selection issues to monitor rather than react to immediately. Sosai misses Gameweek 6 with a tight hamstring but may not be absent for long, while Kevin Sharda picks up an injury against Aston Villa with no timescale yet known. Robinson and Mykolenko are also absent from their squads through injury, although neither is expected to be out for long. Vardial's benching after 490 minutes over the international break may simply be managed rest, but it creates some concern over his security of starts. Kza records DEFCON for the second time this season, a notable improvement on his Aston Villa output. Fulham disappoint again, yet their home fixture against Hull is enough reason to retain faith in Josh King and Gonzalo Garcia for now.
key_points: Triple Captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 7 is the preferred chip play if it remains available.
Hold Bruno Fernandes through his poor run unless his sale is required to finance a stronger move.
João Pedro is back from injury and is a recommended option, while Morgan Rogers has returns in five of six gameweeks.
Savio has played 390 consecutive minutes and remains an encouraging pick despite blanking against Manchester United.
Monitor Sosai, Kevin Sharda, Robinson and Mykolenko for injury updates before selling.
Vardial's benching may be rest after heavy international-break minutes, but it raises a minor rotation concern.
Keep Josh King and Gonzalo Garcia for Fulham's home match against Hull despite the team's recent disappointment.

items.title: BEST SZOBOSZLAI REPLACEMENTS 🎯 | FPL EXPERT GW7 TEAM REVEAL ✅ | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Pascal Gross is Tom Freeman’s priority Gameweek 7 replacement for Szoboszlai
items.summary:
Tom Freeman enters Gameweek 7 with four free transfers and £2.1m in the bank after a strong Wildcard in Gameweek 4. Erling Haaland remains the clear captaincy choice at home to Ipswich, while Cole Palmer is an untouchable premium despite a difficult trip to Everton. Freeman’s squad is generally well set up, but Dominik Szoboszlai becomes the pressing issue after a minor hamstring flag; even if fit, his limited attacking output makes him expendable.

The preferred move is Szoboszlai to Pascal Gross. Gross has three goals, five assists, 53 points and strong underlying numbers, including 11 shots and 18 chances created, while Brighton host Crystal Palace in Gameweek 7. His ownership is already extremely high around the leading ranks, so buying him is as much defensive protection as an attacking move. Brighton’s subsequent matches against Liverpool and Manchester City are not considered prohibitive either, given their form and capacity to score against strong opposition.

Freeman also seriously considers upgrading Barry to Joao Pedro, using the money in the bank to add a third Chelsea attacker alongside Palmer and Morgan Rogers. Chelsea’s run includes Everton, Tottenham, Manchester United, Sunderland and Leeds, and the absence of European football improves the appeal of their attackers. Barry and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall are still viable short-term holds, however, with Chelsea’s defence viewed as vulnerable and Everton’s later fixtures improving; Freeman can bench them for tougher matches such as Arsenal.

A Brighton defensive addition is another option, with Neco Williams a possible sale for a Brighton defender, but it is not essential. If Gross arrives, Freeman is likely to bench Ezri Konsa away to Nottingham Forest, while weighing up Kinsky versus Bart Verbruggen in goal. Other midfielders under consideration include Morgan Gibbs-White for Nottingham Forest’s upcoming Ipswich and Brentford fixtures, Aston Villa’s Manzambi ahead of a better Gameweek 9 run, and Bournemouth’s Tavernier, although European rotation and Bournemouth’s form temper that appeal. Arsenal assets Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard are earmarked more for Gameweek 10, when Arsenal host Hull and captaincy becomes more attractive.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland at home to Ipswich in Gameweek 7, with Palmer retained as a premium cornerstone despite Everton away.
Sell Szoboszlai if his hamstring doubt persists; Gross is the leading replacement because of Brighton’s Crystal Palace fixture, penalties and elite chance-creation numbers.
A double move of Szoboszlai to Gross and Barry to Joao Pedro remains affordable, leaving £0.8m in the bank.
Joao Pedro is appealing as Chelsea begin a strong fixture run and have no European schedule, making a triple Chelsea attack feasible.
Neco Williams to a Brighton defender is an optional third transfer, but Freeman does not need to force the move with four free transfers available.
Bench Konsa away to Nottingham Forest if a Brighton defender arrives, with Morgan Rogers and the Chelsea attackers still playable despite their Everton meeting.
Delay a move for Saka or Odegaard until around Gameweek 10, when Arsenal’s home match against Hull offers a stronger captaincy opportunity.
Monitor Sharda’s shoulder issue, as a longer absence could make Brentford’s Anthony a low-owned differential with improved minutes on the left.
